sections.heading: C - Rules of the Road dossier
sections.markdown:
# C - Rules of the Road dossier

Domain: rules of the road covering flex lanes, freeway use, express lanes, interchanges, intersections, markings, speed, roundabouts, signals, signs, and right of way.

FACT_ID: C-01 | anchor: A01
Flex lane direction is controlled by overhead signals with green arrow to use and red X to avoid.
Why it matters: lane direction can reverse by time of day so driver must check signal before entering.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: C-02 | anchor: A01
Freeway following, U-turn, emergency lane, ramp use and impeding rules govern safe freeway travel.
Why it matters: U-turns, emergency-lane travel, and entrance-ramp exits are prohibited and left-lane impeding can draw citation.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: C-03 | anchor: A02
Express lane free use covers two-or-more occupants plus motorcycles, buses, and registered C-decal clean-fuel vehicles.
Why it matters: single-occupant use without pass or decal is a violation and a common exam trap.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: C-04 | anchor: A02
Double white line crossing is prohibited and express entry or exit is allowed only at dotted access points.
Why it matters: access segments are limited in length and located near interchanges, so early exit planning is required.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: C-05 | anchor: A02
C decal use follows one-time registration payment and windshield placement to the right of the mirror.
Why it matters: only qualifying clean-fuel vehicles may use express lanes toll-free on a single-occupant basis.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: C-06 | anchor: A02
Multi-lane entry uses acceleration lane to match speed then merge and cancel signal, while exit uses early lane choice and steady speed.
Why it matters: late lane changes and speed drops on the main road create rear-end risk.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: C-07 | anchor: A03
Ramp meters show alternating red and green and normally release one vehicle per green unless posted otherwise.
Why it matters: metering is active only when meter-on sign is lit, otherwise drivers enter normally.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: C-08 | anchor: A03
Runaway ramps are for emergency stopping only with no stopping, standing, or parking in ramp or pathway.
Why it matters: blocking a runaway path removes the last safety option for a brake-failure vehicle.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: C-09 | anchor: A03
Single-point interchange U-turn from off-ramp to on-ramp is lawful on green arrow and completed without mid-intersection stop.
Why it matters: the adjacent red arrow faces other traffic, and power loss calls for extreme caution not four-way-stop behavior.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: C-10 | anchor: A04
Intersection approach requires scanning controls and users, full stop behind signs and lines, and no lane change inside.
Why it matters: cross traffic may not yield, so left-right-left check and clear-path confirmation are essential.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: C-11 | anchor: A05
Continuous-flow left uses displaced crossover on signal, while right turns yield and may face restricted red-turn permission.
Why it matters: drivers must watch two left signals and obey posted right-turn controls rather than assuming free right.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: C-12 | anchor: A05
Diverging diamond briefly shifts non-freeway traffic to the opposite side to cut left-turn conflicts at ramps.
Why it matters: unfamiliar alignment demands lane discipline and attention to guide markings.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: C-13 | anchor: A05
Thru-U-turn removes direct lefts by sending drivers through, then to a signalized U-turn and back for a right.
Why it matters: congestion relief depends on drivers accepting longer path instead of turning at the main junction.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: C-14 | anchor: A06
Yellow center markings separate opposite travel and control passing, while white markings separate same-direction flow.
Why it matters: dashed-side permission and double-line prohibition determine lawful passing and express separation.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: C-15 | anchor: A06
Unmarked crosswalks still require stop before the intersection and yield to entering pedestrians.
Why it matters: stop line, crosswalk, or intersection edge defines the stop point at signs and signals.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: C-16 | anchor: A06
Shared center left lane entry is limited in distance before the turn and requires mirror, signal, and blind-spot check.
Why it matters: early entry turns the shared lane into unlawful travel and surprises oncoming left-turn users.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: C-17 | anchor: A07
Basic speed law bars unreasonable speed for conditions, with posted school, business, highway, and rural interstate tiers.
Why it matters: listed limits apply only absent signs or hazards, and poor weather or narrow roads demand slower travel.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: C-18 | anchor: A08
Signal and sign hierarchy places officer commands first, then flashing and steady indications, with work-zone fines doubled.
Why it matters: green does not override an officer stop order, dark signals need full stop and yield, and flaggers must be obeyed.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0056]

High-yield focus: signals and right of way first, then speed and markings, then freeway and express operations.

Misconceptions:
Left lane camping is acceptable when at the limit; correction is move right for overtaking traffic.
Right on red is always allowed; correction is obey posted bans and continuous-flow controls.
Crossing a double white to leave express is minor; correction is wait for dotted access.
Unmarked crosswalks grant no pedestrian right; correction is yield even without paint.
Slow driving is always safe; correction is avoid impeding normal flow.

Mnemonics:
Green means go-check, yellow means soon-red, flashing yellow means careful-yield, flashing red means stop-look.
Flex check: arrow overhead before tire over line.
Express doping: dotted door only, never double white.

Glossary:
Flex lane: time-controlled shared-direction lane governed by overhead signals.
Express lane: high-occupancy corridor with controlled dotted access.
Access point: dotted segment where express entry or exit is permitted.
Ramp meter: alternating ramp signal regulating freeway entry flow.
Shared center lane: middle two-way left-turn lane, not a travel lane.
Diverging diamond: interchange briefly shifting sides to reduce left conflicts.
